acceptance: A workflow test drives the close step against fake open PRs. It closes older same-kind bot PRs, keeps the newest, and leaves a PR alone if it has a non-bot commit or is of the other kind.
The workflow lint tests in tests/unit/workflows pass, and the ledger row for the workflow is updated if its proof changes.
After the next scheduled run, at most one fast-tier and one medium-shard refresh PR are open. #3927 and #4003 (or whatever is stale at that time) are closed with a supersede comment.
Decision gate: if closing needs a token scope the workflow lacks, stop and ask the owner. Do not widen permissions beyond pull-requests: write.
description:
Problem. .github/workflows/fast-duration-baseline-refresh.yml opens a PR on a dated branch (chore/fast-baseline-<date>-<n>, chore/medium-durations-<date>-<n>). It only skips creation when that same branch already has an open PR, so earlier weeks' PRs stay open. On 2026-11-10 the open medium-shard refreshes were #3927 (11-02), #4003 (11-07) and #4065 (11-09), plus #4066 for the fast tier. #3928, the fast-tier refresh, sat unmerged with merge conflicts for five days. Meanwhile develop gained about 2,000 fast tests, every PR's core check ended would-block, and arming stopped repo-wide until an owner stand-in landed a fresh refresh (#4004). Stale refresh PRs cannot merge (they conflict) and hide which one is current.

Change. When the workflow opens a refresh PR, close every older open PR of the same kind (matched by branch prefix) with a comment naming the new PR. Keep the newest. Never close a PR with a non-bot author or with commits added after creation.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate; re-read cited files on current origin/develop first. Never auto-merge refresh PRs and never post review stand-ins; those stay owner-only.
